defect_observations.note: 'The identical argument with Z_n gives nu=Z rho' is a similarly-form step. Counted as written because the argument at l.40-48 applies verbatim and its only measure-specific input (the integral identity for Z_n under rho) is already established at l.36; recorded so a stricter reviewer can see the judgement.

The citation [Example 4.3.7] closes a sentence that includes 'with value zero on null cells'. Example 4.3.7 (p. 229) gives only the ratio on each cell; the zero convention is in source Exercise 4.3.6 (p. 234). Minor locator imprecision.

The title 'The source's strict-positivity tail dichotomy' and the annex title 'Both probabilities in the source tail argument' (annex l.220) can be read as crediting the source with the reciprocal martingale, mu(X=infinity) in {0,1} and the mu~nu form. Source p. 229 proves only nu(X=0) in {0,1} and then concludes 'mu<<nu or mu perp nu'. Body l.191-192 says that the proof includes the reciprocal argument but does not mark it as an extension, and the C014 extension list (l.286-287) leaves it out. Not counted as a failure, because the source does contain a strict-positivity tail dichotomy and the entry never says the reciprocal argument is the source's.

'The bounded mixture route above preserves that source construction': source p. 228 first normalizes mu to a probability by dividing by mu(Omega) and then uses rho=(mu+nu)/2 with Y_n+Z_n=2. The handbook uses rho=(mu+nu)/(c+1) with sum c+1 and never states the source normalization; only l.72 signals the variant. The extension list also omits other handbook additions (the C005 equivalences, the C006 worked examples and the C009 reciprocal argument). The list does not claim to be exhaustive, so this is not counted as a failure.

This audit checked only that the C014 pointer resolves on the route to proved entries for each of Exercises 4.3.4-4.3.10 (pp. 233-234). Whether those proofs are complete is owed by unit ED26-P15-CH-density-and-product-exercises and was not assessed here, so no coverage credit is duplicated.

The finite-dimensional-support boundary is argued in general ('including the divergent-series case') without a concrete divergent instance (for example sigma_m=tau_m=1, a_m-b_m=1). This is plainly realizable, so it is not counted separately from the C012 gap.

This line cites thm:p15-independent-sequence-existence for 'existence and uniqueness'. The corollary's statement gives existence only. Uniqueness comes from thm:p15-kolmogorov-countable (parts/p15/countable-product-measures.tex l.119-133), which its proof applies (annex l.243-249). Minor pointer imprecision.

This step applies thm:p15-vitali-convergence, which assumes a real limit. X is [0,infinity]-valued and finite only nu-almost surely, so a null-set modification is left implicit. This is a correctness-adjacent remark outside the coverage verdict.
